# Release 0 contract fixture corpus

`bin/*.bin` contains committed raw binary fixture bundles. Each bundle uses a test-only 40-byte `R0FXBIN\0` envelope followed by exact raw Boot Entry, handoff, memory-map, and RHD byte sequences. The envelope carries only fixture lengths, expected result, and a provider-fault selector; it is not a RAR OS public contract.

`generate.sh` deterministically recreates every binary from `cases.v1`. `run.sh` compares regenerated bytes with the committed corpus. In the pinned Linux CI route, `reference.rs` is compiled as unsafe-free host-only code and validates the raw bytes with checked unsigned arithmetic. It never dereferences fixture addresses or performs device access.

The binary corpus covers valid x86-64/APIC/16550-I/O and AArch64/GICv3/PL011 values plus malformed framing, alignment, overlap, provider faults, critical records, identity, references, memory maps, controller-relative interrupts, typed register windows, address spaces, authority binding, map/RHD consistency, and architecture agreement.

`validation-precedence.v1` declares one deterministic mutation for every one of the 36 artifact-qualified predicates, all 35 adjacent edges, and eight security-sensitive non-adjacent fault pairs. `conformance-scenarios.v1` adds both-architecture cases for entry/descriptor aliasing, descriptor reordering, short and faulting providers, compatible minors, unknown critical additions, cardinality/model failures, CPU references, map limits, access logs, and rejected effects.

The host oracle uses a descriptor-keyed instrumented provider. It proves the exact permitted access sequence and rejects a second copy of any source. A separate effect sink proves rejected inputs do not clear entropy, activate trace, or construct device authority. Target-decoder agreement remains an R0-003/R0-004 obligation because no target decoder exists in R0-002.
